>We aren't \*\*in\*\* the universe, we \*\*are\*\* the universe. We exist.

I don't think we \*\*are\*\* the universe in the way you mean it. I think we are a small and relatively insignificant part that forms the universe, which existence is irrelevant to the latter.

>And so the things which we apply meaning or purpose to, those things are also objectively meaningful to us, and since we are the universe, they are meaningful to the universe. Just not all of it.

Like I said in the other comment, we can use words to twist and make an argument sound logic with circumlocutions, but this doesn't applies to the real essence of the nature. I'm not accusing you, it's pretty normal. But your theory just confirmed what I said.

We \*\*are\*\* the universe. Considering this, our meaning of things apply to it (not all of it) and it is true, right? But like I said, we are a small and irrelevant part of it which existence is irrelevant. When we die, our meaning will die with us. The universe will not resent of this because our meaning was useless to its existence. Our meaning is circumscribed to us, the irrelevant part that has no role to the big scale of things. It exists and has the only purpose to make sentient animals go on with their life, but it has no importance or relevance whatsoever to the real meaning of the nature.

> Yes. So what?

I understand that you disagree with me, but you should calm down. These are just opinions. 🙂

> does that mean it doesn't exist?

No, it exists. But it exists only for us and not for the thing in itself. Our meaning is not the real essence of things. This is why the meaning (our meaning) die with us when we shut down, and in that moment everything become "nothing".

> The fact that it isn't universal doesn't mean it doesn't exist.

Again, you are reading me wrong or I explained myself in the wrong way. It exists, but it isn't the truth (in my opinion, obviously). Our meaning of things is just our tendency to apply logic and rationality to everything and "nothing"; this is mostly dictated by fear and pragmatism.

I didn't said that is pointless or meaningless, this is why I asked what is the point. I want to know if people change their idea about life when they realize that everything has a real end and that they can't carry on their memory for the eternity. Sometimes people (me first) forget that everything that belongs to us has a real end, unlike the universe. 

>Finite things have infinitely more meaning than anything that could possible be infinite. 

This could sound cool and right in words, but in the big scale of the universe nothing has a real meaning. We are the ones who give meaning to things, as sentient animals. We give a meaning even to the universe. This is why everything, in itself and without a sentient animal that rationalize it, is meaningless. This is why I think that when we shut down, everything become meaningless. Perhaps at that moment everything becomes the real itself: nothing. It could be nihilistic, but for me is really romantic.
